questions.question: For the matrix [latex]p=\begin{bmatrix} 3 & -2&2 \\ 0& -2 & 1\\ 0 &0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}[/latex] one of the eigen values is equal to -2. Which of the following is an eigen vector ?
questions.explanation:
Since matrix is triangular, the eigen values are the diagonal elements themselves namely [latex]\lambda =3, -2[/latex] and 1. Corresponding to eigen value [latex]\lambda = -2[/latex] let us find the eigen vector [latex][A-\lambda I]\hat{x}=0[/latex] [latex]\begin{bmatrix} 3-\lambda & -2 & 2\\ 0 & -2-\lambda & 1\\ 0& 0 & 1-\lambda \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x_1\\ x_2\\ x_3 \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 0\\ 0\\ 0 \end{bmatrix}[/latex] Putting  [latex]\lambda = -2[/latex] in above equation we get, [latex]\begin{bmatrix} 5 & -2 & 2\\ 0 & 0 & 1\\ 0& 0 & 3\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x_1\\ x_2\\ x_3 \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 0\\ 0\\ 0 \end{bmatrix}[/latex] Which gives the equations, [latex]\begin{aligned} 5x_1-2x_2+2x_3&=0 \;\;...(i)\\ x_3 &=0 \;\;...(ii)\\ 3x_3&=0 \;\;...(iii) \end{aligned}[/latex] Since equation (ii) and (iii) are same we have [latex]\begin{aligned} 5x_1-2x_2+2x_3&=0 \;\;...(i)\\ x_3 &=0 \;\;...(ii)\end{aligned}[/latex]
Putting [latex]x_2=k[/latex], we get [latex]x_3=0, x_2=k[/latex] and [latex]5x_1-2k+2 \times 0=0[/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow \;x_1=2/5 \;k[/latex] Eigen vectors are of the form [latex]\begin{bmatrix} x_1\\ x_2\\ x_3 \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 2/5 k\\ k\\ 0 \end{bmatrix}[/latex] [latex]\begin{aligned} x_1:x_2:x_3&=2/5k:k:0\\ &=2/5:1:0\\ &=2:5:0 \end{aligned}[/latex] [latex]\therefore \;\;\begin{bmatrix} x_1\\ x_2\\ x_3 \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 2\\ 5\\ 0 \end{bmatrix}[/latex] is an eigen vector of matrix p.
questions.explanation_html:
Since matrix is triangular, the eigen values are the diagonal elements themselves namely [latex]\lambda =3, -2[/latex] and 1.
Corresponding to eigen value [latex]\lambda = -2[/latex] let us find the eigen vector
[latex][A-\lambda I]\hat{x}=0[/latex]
[latex]\begin{bmatrix} 3-\lambda & -2 & 2\\ 0 & -2-\lambda & 1\\ 0& 0 & 1-\lambda \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x_1\\ x_2\\ x_3 \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 0\\ 0\\ 0 \end{bmatrix}[/latex]
Putting [latex]\lambda = -2[/latex] in above equation we get,
[latex]\begin{bmatrix} 5 & -2 & 2\\ 0 & 0 & 1\\ 0& 0 & 3\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x_1\\ x_2\\ x_3 \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 0\\ 0\\ 0 \end{bmatrix}[/latex]
Which gives the equations,
[latex]\begin{aligned} 5x_1-2x_2+2x_3&=0 \;\;...(i)\\ x_3 &=0 \;\;...(ii)\\ 3x_3&=0 \;\;...(iii) \end{aligned}[/latex]
Since equation (ii) and (iii) are same we have
[latex]\begin{aligned} 5x_1-2x_2+2x_3&=0 \;\;...(i)\\ x_3 &=0 \;\;...(ii)\end{aligned}[/latex] Putting [latex]x_2=k[/latex], we get
[latex]x_3=0, x_2=k[/latex] and [latex]5x_1-2k+2 \times 0=0[/latex]
[latex]\Rightarrow \;x_1=2/5 \;k[/latex]
Eigen vectors are of the form
[latex]\begin{bmatrix} x_1\\ x_2\\ x_3 \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 2/5 k\\ k\\ 0 \end{bmatrix}[/latex]
[latex]\begin{aligned} x_1:x_2:x_3&=2/5k:k:0\\ &=2/5:1:0\\ &=2:5:0 \end{aligned}[/latex]
[latex]\therefore \;\;\begin{bmatrix} x_1\\ x_2\\ x_3 \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 2\\ 5\\ 0 \end{bmatrix}[/latex] is an eigen vector of matrix p.

questions.question: If [latex]R=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0&-1 \\ 2& 1 & -1\\ 2&3 & 2 \end{bmatrix}[/latex], then top row of [latex]R^{-1}[/latex] is

[latex]\begin{aligned} R &=\begin{bmatrix} 1 &0 &-1 \\ 2 & 1 & -1\\ 2& 3& 2 \end{bmatrix} \\ R^{-1} &=\frac{adj(R)}{|R|}=\frac{[\text{cofator }(R)]^T}{|R|} \\ |R|&=\begin{vmatrix} 1 &0 &-1 \\ 2 & 1 & -1\\ 2 & 3& 2 \end{vmatrix} \\ &=1(2+3)-0(4+2)-1(6-2) \\ &= 5-4=1 \end{aligned}[/latex] Since we need only the top row of [latex]R^{-1}[/latex], we need to find only first column of (R) which after transpose will become first row of Adj(A). [latex]\begin{aligned}
 \text{co-factor of (1,1)}&=+\begin{vmatrix}
1 &-1 \\ 
3 & 2
\end{vmatrix} \\ 
 &=2+3=5 \\ 
 \text{co-factor of (2,1)}&=+\begin{vmatrix}
0 &-1 \\ 
1 & -1
\end{vmatrix}=-3 \\ 
\text{co-factor of (3,1)}&=+\begin{vmatrix}
0 &-1 \\ 
1 & -1
\end{vmatrix}=+1\\
\therefore \;\text{ co-factor of (A)} &= \begin{bmatrix}
5 &-  &- \\ 
-3 & - &- \\ 
 1& - & -
\end{bmatrix}\\ 
 Adj(A)&= [cof.(A)]^T\\ 
 &= \begin{bmatrix}
5 &-3  &1 \\ 
- & - &- \\ 
 -& - & -
\end{bmatrix}\\ 
\text{Dividing by |R|} &= 1 \text{ gives}\\ 
 R^{-1}&= \begin{bmatrix}
5 &-3  &1 \\ 
- & - &- \\ 
 -& - & -
\end{bmatrix}\\ 
 \therefore \;\; \text{top row of }R^{-1}&=[5\;-3\;1]
\end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question:
A fair coin is tossed three times in succession. If the first toss produces a head,
then the probability of getting exactly two heads in three tosses is
questions.explanation: [latex]\begin{aligned} P(A|B)&=\frac{P(A\cap B)}{P(B)}\\ \therefore \; &P(\text{2 heads in 3 tosses }| \text{ first toss is head})\\ &=\frac{P(\text{3 heads in 3 tosses and first toss is head})}{P(\text{ first toss is head})}\\ &=P(\text{ first toss is head})\\ &=\frac{1}{2}\\ &P(\text{2 heads in 3 tosses and first toss is head})\\ &=P(HHT)+P(HTH)\\ &=\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} +\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} =\frac{1}{4}\\ \therefore \;&\text{ Required probability}=\frac{1/4}{1/2}=\frac{1}{2} \end{aligned}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html: [latex]\begin{aligned} P(A|B)&=\frac{P(A\cap B)}{P(B)}\\ \therefore \; &P(\text{2 heads in 3 tosses }| \text{ first toss is head})\\ &=\frac{P(\text{3 heads in 3 tosses and first toss is head})}{P(\text{ first toss is head})}\\ &=P(\text{ first toss is head})\\ &=\frac{1}{2}\\ &P(\text{2 heads in 3 tosses and first toss is head})\\ &=P(HHT)+P(HTH)\\ &=\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} +\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} =\frac{1}{4}\\ \therefore \;&\text{ Required probability}=\frac{1/4}{1/2}=\frac{1}{2} \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question: For the function [latex]f (x) = x^{2}e^{x}[/latex], the maximum occurs when [latex]x[/latex] is equal to
questions.explanation: [latex]\begin{aligned} f(x)&=x^2e^{-x}\\ f'(x)&=x^2(-e^{-x})+e^{-x} \times 2x\\ &=e^{-x}(2x-x^2)\\ \text{Putting, } f'(x)&=0\\ e^{-x}(2x-x^2)&=0\\ e^{-x}x(2-x)&=0\\ \end{aligned}[/latex] [latex] x =0 [/latex] or  [latex] x=2[/latex] are the stationary points. [latex]\begin{aligned} \text{Now, } f''(x) &= e^{-x}(2-2x)+(2x-x^2)(-e^{-x})\\ &= e^{-x}(2-2x-(2x-x^2))\\ &= e^{-x}(x^2-4x+2)\\ At\;x=0& \\ f''(0)&= e^{-0}(0-0+2)=2 \end{aligned}[/latex] Since [latex]f''(x)=2[/latex] is [latex]\gt 0[/latex] at [latex]x=0[/latex] we have a minima. Now at [latex]x=2[/latex] [latex] \begin{aligned} f''(2)&=e^{-2}(2^2-4\times 2 +2) \\ &=-2e^{-2} \lt 0 \end{aligned} [/latex] [latex]\therefore \;\; At \;\; x=2[/latex] we have a maxima.

Since [latex]f''(x)=2[/latex] is [latex]\gt 0[/latex] at [latex]x=0[/latex] we have a minima.
Now at [latex]x=2[/latex]

Putting [latex]x_2=k[/latex], we get [latex]x_3=0, x_2=k[/latex] and [latex]5x_1-2k+2 \times 0=0[/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow \;x_1=2/5 \;k[/latex] Eigen vectors are of the form [latex]\begin{bmatrix} x_1\\ x_2\\ x_3 \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 2/5 k\\ k\\ 0 \end{bmatrix}[/latex] [latex]\begin{aligned} x_1:x_2:x_3&=2/5k:k:0\\ &=2/5:1:0\\ &=2:5:0 \end{aligned}[/latex] [latex]\therefore \;\;\begin{bmatrix} x_1\\ x_2\\ x_3 \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 2\\ 5\\ 0 \end{bmatrix}[/latex] is an eigen vector of matrix p.
